Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

yourhonor 0.1.0

  • Initial CRAN submission. yourhonor treats an LLM-as-judge as a measurement instrument: it calibrates the judge blind against human raters, puts an interval on every estimate, probes it for bias and test-retest stability, and lets an explicit acceptance policy decide what the evidence supports.

Calibration and agreement

  • calibrate_judge() compares a judge’s labels with one or more human raters, either from a live judge function or from labels already in the data. A live judge sees only the columns named in input_cols; human columns and the judge-label column are refused as inputs. Items are shuffled before grading and keyed with a fresh opaque .item_id, keyed output is validated and restored to source order, and both key spaces are kept (.item_id, .judge_item_id and a blinding_map) so judge-side logs can be joined back without un-blinding the run.
  • With several raters the reference label is the modal consensus (ties are excluded and counted), and human-human reliability is reported as a benchmark, not a ceiling. Judge abstentions (NA labels) are reported separately from human gaps, with a Clopper-Pearson interval on the abstention rate.
  • agreement() reports Cohen’s kappa, Krippendorff’s alpha, and Gwet’s AC1 (nominal) or AC2 (weighted) with item-bootstrap intervals over a fixed label universe, explicit missingness and an explicit status for degenerate data. Point estimates come from irrCAC; the bootstrap scores each resample natively, with identical draws, in bounded memory.
  • Each coefficient also carries conf_low_exact, a resampling-free finite-sample lower bound on its observed agreement mapped onto the coefficient’s scale. A boundary-degenerate bootstrap (a zero-width interval at perfect agreement) is flagged unreliable rather than read as certainty. vignette("exact-bound") derives the bound.
  • confusion() and confusion_metrics() give the confusion matrix in the declared label order with per-class support, precision and recall and exact intervals; plot_confusion() draws it with ggplot2.

Bias probes

  • probe_bias() runs pointwise verbosity, self-preference and bandwagon probes in one blind, randomised batch. probe_position() swaps candidate columns through neutral display slots and maps each choice back to the stable candidate identity.
  • Every probe reports its flip rate, a net directional rate with a conservative interval, a sign-test p-value adjusted across the multiple-comparison family, raw missingness and a verdict. A large but balanced flip rate is reported but never flagged as bias.
  • combine_bias() merges probe runs under one multiple-comparison family.

Stability

  • test_retest() re-grades items and reports mean pairwise disagreement between runs with a conservative interval, a chance-corrected stability coefficient, and an any-flip rate tied explicitly to the number of runs.
  • It also reports a worst-case pairwise disagreement in which every pair involving a missing re-run judgment disagrees, so abstaining where the judge is unstable cannot hide instability.

Acceptance policies and reports

  • acceptance_policy() makes every threshold a declared parameter: sample size, class support, agreement, per-class recall and precision, missingness and abstention, probe and stability requirements. A threshold supplied without the gate that reads it is an error.
  • report() turns the evidence into PASS, FAIL, NOT_ASSESSED or INDETERMINATE, check by check, with numeric value, op and threshold columns. Missing evidence is never reported as a pass, and unscored probe items and missing re-run judgments count against the judge in the bounds a policy assesses. Without a policy the report is descriptive. It prints to the console or renders as Markdown, and its agreement and stability headlines show the bound the policy assesses beside the observed interval.
  • Every piece of evidence can carry an audit_id, and report() refuses to bind evidence tagged for a different judge.

Audit artifacts and vitals

  • write_audit() writes a Markdown report or a versioned, language-neutral JSON summary (yourhonor.audit.v1) that omits item rows. ?write_audit documents every field. A field’s JSON number type never changes between runs: counts are integers and every other number is written as a decimal.
  • audit_vitals() and stability_vitals() reuse grades and epochs already present in a vitals task without another model call; stability_vitals() refuses epochs whose judge-visible content changed.
  • vignette("yourhonor") walks through an audit end to end, with further vignettes on bias probes, stability and vitals, and policies and audit artifacts; an article on the package website shows how to wrap an ellmer chat as a judge.

Errors and missing values

  • Errors carry classes by family (yourhonor_input_error, yourhonor_judge_error, yourhonor_policy_error, yourhonor_binding_error), each also of class yourhonor_error, so a caller can catch a family without matching message text (see ?yourhonor-errors).
  • A missing label is NA everywhere: a numeric NaN from a judge, a precomputed rating column or a vitals score is missing, never the label "NaN", and empty or whitespace-only labels are refused.

Data

  • support_gold is an eight-item synthetic dataset for API demonstration.
  • synthetic_gold is a 200-item synthetic dataset with three simulated raters, sized so an audit can reach a verdict. Every label is planted and the text is templated; it is not a benchmark.
